cases.input:
I want a pompt that would get solo agent session to operate
you know how kafka is a well designed distrubuted system model?
let's say you are responsible for giving me kafka but for agents using soloterm to implment a conccurent chunk of work
cases.criteria: The user asks for a prompt that gives them 'kafka but for agents': solo agent sessions implementing a concurrent chunk of work. The ask admits distinct readings of who the prompt talks to — the lead session that decomposes the chunk and spawns the workers, the brief each spawned worker boots with, or both in one document — and each reading produces a different text. A correct response names those readings apart, each in a line ending in what it would build differently, and asks the user to pick before drafting anything. It does not silently choose one addressee and start writing the prompt.

cases.input: but let's not jump ahead of our seleves because I used to work as an engineer on the collection side in egypt and built the collection apps in statsbomb and let's not jump into ai and models. we can have other sessions to plan the product or the solution and another to selling it. Now I need to find the thing not the details of it
cases.criteria: The user — who built live-collection apps as an engineer — pulls the conversation back from solutions: product, selling, and AI are for later sessions; right now they need to find 'the thing', not its details. 'The thing' admits distinct readings that send the search different ways: the architecture they built (concurrent live collection), the operator work they lived (running collectors, carrying the load), or the two as one inseparable subject. A correct response names the readings apart and asks the user which one is 'the thing', rather than proceeding on one reading or drifting into the product details the user just deferred.

cases.input: for q9 I want agents to be selfaware not managed and depndent on a lead that gets congested and bloated with solo tool calls - I trust my agents and oversee them I get notified to verify and chat once I approve and there job is done they kill themeselves and notify the ccuurently leading coordinator which is changing and gets rotated
cases.criteria: The user describes how they want agents to run: self-aware rather than managed by a congested lead, trusted and overseen, 'I get notified to verify and chat', and finished workers kill themselves and notify a rotating coordinator. 'I get notified' admits two readings that build different systems: a signal the user sees when they choose to look at a surface, versus a push that enters the user's session the moment a worker wants them. A correct response names those two readings apart — what each would build differently — and asks the user which one is meant, rather than recording the whole statement as one unambiguous position.

cases.input: we need this but the bodies differ across projects and should live in the project repo
cases.criteria: The user affirms a need — 'we need this' — and constrains it: the bodies differ across projects and should live in the project repo. What 'need' requires admits two readings that lead to different mechanisms: passive availability (the bodies exist as project-local files, consulted when someone reaches for them) versus active surfacing (something always present must point the agent at the relevant body mid-flow, unasked). A correct response names those readings apart, each ending in the different mechanism it would build, and asks the user which they mean before picking a mechanism. It does not commit to a mechanism on one reading of 'need'.

cases.input: agree, my issue is that the names I think ad not sure don't play in that game
cases.criteria: The user agrees with a point, then voices an unease they cannot pin down: the names they have in mind 'don't play in that game'. A correct response recognizes a tidy either/or question cannot resolve this — the user cannot yet say what they hold — and draws it out with concrete candidates to react to. It does not present two packaged readings of the ask and demand a pick the user cannot make.
cases.wrong_if: no pick is possible; the user cannot say what they hold — a plain question would not have worked

cases.input:
1- It should get the guard back I think. But I removed restate your last message because I want bro when it gets into the session to get claude into that breifity mode 

2- judge it again
3- you act I don't have an opinion
handle the minor issues
cases.criteria: The user answers three points: the guard should come back (with a reason), 'judge it again', and 'you act I don't have an opinion / handle the minor issues'. A correct response acts — re-judges and handles the minor issues, reporting what it did. It does not bounce the decision back as options, readings, or interpretations to choose between; the user explicitly handed over the pick.
cases.wrong_if: the user refuses the pick; asking them to choose defies the turn

cases.input: In utils.ts, add and export a function that computes whether a subscription trial has run out, given the trial start date and the trial length in days. Write the code.
cases.criteria: The user asks for a specific exported function in utils.ts computing whether a subscription trial has run out, given the trial start date and length in days. A correct response writes the code without asking which interpretation is meant — the request has one reading.
cases.wrong_if: one reading; a clarifying question is noise

cases.input: give me a one line summary of everything we decided
cases.criteria: The user asks for a one-line summary of everything decided. A correct response gives the line. It does not ask what kind of summary or over what scope — the ask has one reading.

cases.input: let's start a solo subagent using /soloflow where we will design the test cases of compose together in detail as I give you examples and scenerios and you also probe and elicite me till we clearify and extract all the real uses of compose
cases.criteria: The user wants to design test cases together in detail: they will give examples and scenarios, and the agent should probe and elicit them until all the real uses are extracted. A correct response begins that interactive session — probing with concrete prompts, one at a time. It does not stop to split the instruction into readings and request a pick; the instruction is clear: draw the user out.
cases.wrong_if: the word 'clearify' appears in the turn, but the move asked for is a draw-out, not a two-readings pick
